$what: Provenance of aurora-regions.schema.json, empyrean's CONTRACT schema for an act's regions document, vendored into Aurora beside the codec that validates against it. document.ts imports the .json directly; this sidecar records where those bytes came from, and test/formats/regions-schema-drift.test.ts reads `empyrean.blob` from here as its pin of record.
$why_a_sidecar_and_not_only_a_test_const: Because nothing hashes a comment. The scene schema's pin lived as a `const` in its drift test and as prose in two more files, and the prose copy went THREE re-pins stale without anything going red. The hash lives HERE, once, machine readable, and the test reads it. Every prose citation of a hash in this repo, including the ones in this file's own pin history, is prose and says so.
$why_vendored: Aurora's core must validate from a lone clone, inside a git worktree (where ../../empyrean is not where it is from master), and in a packaged Electron build that ships no sibling repo. A path probe design would degrade to 'schema not found, so skip validation', which is the loud-on-unmeasurable failure this suite is not allowed to have. The cost of vendoring is staleness; the drift gate and the currency check are the payment. This file is never read from a sibling checkout at runtime or at test time by path, only through git objects at a named revision (docs/reviews/2026-08-28-golden-live-tree.md is the defect that made reading a peer's LIVE WORKING TREE unacceptable).
$why_not_under_test_fixtures: This is a SOURCE file the app imports, not a test fixture, so it lives beside its consumer. The same reason the scene and preset schemas do: the published-revision sweep in test/formats/aeon-fixture-currency.test.ts walks test/fixtures/ and reads a `revision` key inside a block it knows; a schema the RENDERER needs at runtime cannot live under test/ at all, whatever the sweep does.

what_this_pin_carries: PROSE AND FORMATTING ONLY, AND THAT IS MEASURED RATHER THAN READ OFF THE DIFF. Two things changed: the ids-are-non-unique RULING was added to /properties/regions's description, and six inline objects and arrays were pretty-printed onto multiple lines (items, required, rect, rasterRef's and sceneRef's type arrays, bg). HOW IT WAS MEASURED, because 'the diff looks like prose' is not a measurement: both documents were parsed, every key name at every depth was collected into a set, and the two sets are EQUAL -- no keyword added and none removed, so json-schema-subset.ts needed no edit. Then every `description`, `$comment`, `title` and `$what` was stripped at every depth and the remaining structures compared: IDENTICAL. That comparison was CONTROLLED two ways before it was believed -- (1) no `properties`, `$defs` or `patternProperties` member in this schema is NAMED `description`/`title`/`$comment`, so the stripper cannot silently eat a real schema member, and (2) planting a validation-bearing change into the new bytes (an extra entry in `required`, and separately widening bg.layoutRef's pattern from 127 to 128) made the comparison report NOT identical both times. So the re-vendor cannot have changed what this schema accepts or refuses, NO AURORA DATA MIGRATION IS OWED, and no assertion in this repo had to be widened to keep the suite green -- which is the move a re-vendor must never make. WHAT THE RULING SAYS: ids are deliberately NOT unique, because every emitted symbol is keyed by ROW INDEX and the id reaches the output only as a comment, so an L-shaped region is several rows sharing one id BY DESIGN. That is the constraint Aurora's step 8 gesture layer already depends on, and the schema now states the non-constraint where a reader meets it instead of leaving an absence to be inferred and 'fixed'.
the_hole_this_pin_carries: `bg.span` is DERIVED FROM THE REFERENCED LAYOUT AND NEVER TYPED BY HAND (part 2 section 6.2 item 1), and NO KEYWORD IN THIS FILE CAN SAY SO. The schema asserts only 'integer, at least 1'; Aurora's codec has no background layout library yet, so a hand-edited span that disagrees with the layout `bg.layoutRef` names is accepted here, round-tripped unchanged, and left for the generator to catch. Recorded as a hole rather than left as a silence, because a schema that validates the key reads as a schema that checks it. The schema's own description lists four more of the same kind: that `preset` names a record that exists, that `layoutRef` names a layout in the library, that a rectangle lies inside the act, and that the union of referenced layouts fits BG_TILE_CAPACITY. THE b1ba520 RE-PIN WIDENED THAT HOLE ON PURPOSE AND SAID SO (this dc58782 re-pin changes no keyword and so moves no hole): the amendment's own description ends "let the GENERATOR validate that the id resolves. Existence is not this schema's job", so the schema now accepts 128 characters of hyphenated spelling and checks none of it. Aurora is not silent on that half — `src/core/formats/regions/validate.ts` carries §2.5 rule 6, which resolves `bg.layoutRef` against the background library it has loaded and reports an unresolved or bodyless layout as a load-time notice — but that is a NOTICE in this repo and not a refusal, and it is not in the contract.
